title: Analysis of platelets as well as cellular and cell-free markers in scleroderma, graft-versus-host disease (GvHD), and other immunological diseases.
summary: Trotz der bekannten immunmodulierenden Effekte der extrakorporalen Photopherese (ECP) sind ihre Auswirkungen auf zellfreie DNA (cfDNA) sowie auf reife und retikulierte Thrombozyten bislang nur unzureichend untersucht. Da Thrombozyten leicht aktivierbar sind und eng mit Immunzellen wie Monozyten und dendritischen Zellen interagieren, könnten sie die Reaktion dieser Zellen auf cfDNA beeinflussen. Dadurch könnten sie eine wichtige Rolle bei den immunologischen Effekten der ECP spielen. Die Untersuchung dieser Mechanismen könnte neue Einblicke in die Wirkweise der ECP liefern und unreife Thrombozyten als mögliche Biomarker identifizieren.

interventions.name:
Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma)

Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of systemic sclerosis.
blood Assessments are performed before extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP), immediately after ECP, and at 6-month follow-up.

Graft-versus-Host Disease (GvHD) and other immunological diseases

Patients with GvHD or other immunological diseases, including acute Sézary syndrome, T-cell lymphoma, psoriasis, and pemphigus.
blood Assessments are performed before ECP, after ECP, and at 6-month follow-up.

Healthy Controls

Healthy individuals without a family history of autoimmune or malignant disease, and without current or previous immunomodulatory or oncological therapy.
Single baseline blood sampling only (no ECP, no follow-up measurements).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis: systemic sclerosis (scleroderma); healthy controls without family history of autoimmune or malignant disease, without evidence of immune activation or current/previous cancer therapy; graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) or other immunological diseases such as acute Sézary syndrome and T-cell lymphoma, psoriasis, and pemphigus

Planned treatment with extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP)

Written informed consent to participate

Age over 18 years

Ability to read and understand the German language is required
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of informed consent
Smoking or alcohol abuse
Active infection or other contraindications to blood sampling
Cardiovascular or thrombotic diseases, including myocardial infarction, stroke, venous thrombosis, or peripheral arterial disease within the last 12 months; chronic heart failure NYHA class III–IV
BMI > 30 kg/m² (obesity)
Diabetes mellitus: known type 1 or type 2 diabetes or HbA1c > 6.5%
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Continuous anticoagulant therapy (e.g., phenprocoumon/Marcumar, direct oral anticoagulants, heparin)
Platelet disorders
